correctness.rationale: Complete facet classification: two cap planes at distance h and 2n lateral triangles (n rectangles at aligned twist), all at common explicit distance D; centered hull-inradius equals cosine of spherical mesh norm since origin is interior. Squaring D>=h yields x<=ct/(1+ct). In the other branch D^2 is decreasing beyond the switch because its maximum is at (t-c)/(2+t-c) strictly below ct/(1+ct) for c>=1/2. This proves the unique optimum at each twist and at half-step twist globally. 245 independent convex hull comparisons, 300000 random directions and 25 local-optimum checks passed. Quantifiers cover n>=3, 0<h<1 and all twists in a full period. Finite checks are only corroboration.

value.rationale: The largest empty cap (mesh norm) of two regular sampling rings is a natural geometric design invariant. The theorem provides a complete two-parameter phase diagram and optimizes both latitude and phase for every ring cardinality, distinguishing polar holes from side holes. It unexpectedly proves all edge-uniform antiprisms with n>=4 are suboptimal within their own two-ring class, and that even as 2n grows the best two-ring mesh norm has a nonzero limiting angle pi/4; these structural features motivate the exact values beyond a textbook one-off computation.
